newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slips after Buba tender award.
newsitem.headline: German call money slips after Buba tender award.

text.p: German call money rates slipped slightly on Wednesday after the Bundesbank injected net funds at its weekly tender award, but rates were not expected to slip below the three percent main market rate, dealers said.
"We are trading a little bit lower today," said a senior dealer in Frankfurt, adding however that conditions were sluggish leaving little hope for any major move.
Call money traded between 3.00/3.05 this morning with the bulk of turnover conducted around 3.01/3.02 percent. This compares with Tuesday's 3.02/3.03 percent rates.
The Bundesbank on Wednesday injected a net 800 million marks into the system, slightly more than what the market had expected, dealers said.
"The Bundesbank is giving us ample liquidity and we get the feeling they are more comfortable having the market trade closer to the three percent repo level," another trader said.

But traders also said this in now way should give rise to speculation the Bundesbank might be preparing an interest rate cut. Economists polled by Reuters unanimously said they expected the central bank would leave all three key rates unchanged at Thursday's council meeting.
Dealers also said they were feeling comfortable with reserve data, which showed an improvement on Tuesday.

Banks held 39.6 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Tuesday, up from 37.8 billion marks held one day earlier. The monthly average however was slightly lower at 40.3 billion marks, compared with 40.4 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings were negligible on Tuesday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate FIONA= stood at 3.04333 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.05500 percent on Tuesday.
